newsitem.title: UK: UK Cruise missile site handed back to people.
newsitem.headline: UK Cruise missile site handed back to people.

text.p: Greenham Common, the U.S. military airbase that became a focus of anti-nuclear protests by women, was handed back to the people on Tuesday for use as a park and business centre.
Greenham Common became a rallying point for protesters against Cruise nuclear missiles in the early 1980s with 50,000 women surrounding the site at one point.

But the missiles finally left six years ago at the end of the Cold War and the base was bought by the Greenham Common Trust, made up of the local Newbury District Council and a consortium of businesses.

"It's the end of 50 years of the shadow that has been cast by military activity on Greenham Common and made it famous throughout Europe. It's over and now we are moving into the future," said Sir Michael Peters of the Greenham Common Trust.
Most of the 850 acres (350 Hectares) of parkland are being returned to the public for walks and recreation. Some buildings are being turned into business units.
But the huge bunkers that housed the Cruise missiles must remain under the terms of the disarmament treaty which allows the Russians to inspect the site at any time should they choose.
The Greenham Common Women have also not entirely disappeared. A small convoy of caravans nestles under a "peace camp" banner near the old gates of the site.
"This is a very important place for women to come to and take non-violent direct action against the Trident nuclear weapons system," one of the peace camp residents told reporters.
